### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be35f992fd5154809e15b8b423f8a7ee35d87c54` — the merge of head `8d3ba747cdcd6b703b09b4c07622d924c3a7eb3e` into base `45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be35f992fd5154809e15b8b423f8a7ee35d87c54 && git checkout be35f992fd5154809e15b8b423f8a7ee35d87c54
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb 8d3ba747cdcd6b703b09b4c07622d924c3a7eb3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb && git merge --no-ff 8d3ba747cdcd6b703b09b4c07622d924c3a7eb3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8d3ba747cdcd6b703b09b4c07622d924c3a7eb3e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-connections.ts (`markReconnectRequired`, `resolveRefreshToken`, `resolveRegisteredClient`), packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-connection.object.ts (`status`, `status_reason`), packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/grant-handle.ts (`RECONNECT_REQUIRED_CAUSES`, `reconnectRequiredReason`, `grantRefused`, `endpointOf`, `refreshOnce`, `get` / `refresh`), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (the MCP tool-discovery mark at the `markReconnectRequired` call) and .changeset/28961-connector-connection-status-doc.md

Read-only round: the net diff against `main` at the merge base `104cd1a5` (2 files, +13 / −3, the same two files the PR's file list names), card #28961's body and all three comments, PR #29238's body and file list, and the check-runs on `8d3ba747` (every required context `success`; the skipped rows are opt-in or path-filtered legs). The dispatching seat's ACCEPT record and landing note are not inputs. Every cited file was read at `8d3ba747`, never on the working tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The net change is one JSDoc arm rewrapped and a changeset; no type, export, `.describe()` or runtime string moves — right.** The `ConnectorConnectionState.status` union is byte-identical (`'not_connected' | 'connected' | 'reconnect_required'`); only the comment lines above it change. A JSDoc on an interface field is not a `.describe()`, so `content/docs/references/**` is not owed and `check:docs` has nothing to regenerate; the `TypeScript Type Check` leg (home of `check:generated` and `check:api-surface`) is green on this head.
2. **Dropping "expired" is the correct reading of the runtime — right.** In `grant-handle.ts`, `get()` refreshes whenever the cached token is absent, stale, or cached under a different `revision` than the row carries, and `refresh()` (the 401 retry of `callWithBorrowedCredential`) refreshes unconditionally; `refreshOnce` then reaches `no_refresh_token` the moment `resolveRefreshToken` answers `undefined`, and `no_client` the moment `endpointOf` does. Neither path reads `expires_at`. A fresh replica, a moved revision or a 401 therefore marks a no-refresh-token connection while its access token may still be valid, which is what the card states and what the runtime's own comment at `RECONNECT_REQUIRED_CAUSES` records ("Not 'expired': a refresh also runs on a cache miss ... and on a dispatch's 401").
3. **The three arms enumerate every path that writes `reconnect_required` — right.** `markReconnectRequired` has exactly two callers in the tree: `grantRefused` in `grant-handle.ts` (reached with the three `ReconnectRequiredCause` values `refused`, `no_refresh_token`, `no_client`) and the MCP tool-discovery handler in `plugin.ts` (`discoveryTokenRefusedReason`, written only while the row is still `connected` under the same `connectedAt`). The JSDoc's first arm is `refused`, its second arm names both `no_refresh_token` and `no_client` in its parenthesis, its third arm is the discovery mark. Nothing is left out and nothing is invented.
4. **"no refresh token was issued" is exact, not an overclaim — right.** `resolveRefreshToken` answers `undefined` only when `record.hasRefreshToken` is false; a stored token that cannot be read back (no crypto provider, no privileged dereference) throws `ConnectorCredentialUnavailableError` and is never turned into a mark, which the store's docblock states in so many words. "no client to refresh with" is likewise `endpointOf` answering `undefined`: no declared `tokenUrl` + `clientId`, and no registered client the row keeps.
5. **"`statusReason` says which" holds.** `markReconnectRequired` writes `status_reason: reason`, `toRecord` carries it as `statusReason`, and the door's state is read from the record; a legacy row storing none is answered with the `refused` sentence by `markedReason`, which is the optional member's documented absence case.
6. **The three carriers of the same fact now read the same sentence — right.** `connector-connections.ts` L325–329, `sys-connector-connection.object.ts` L98 and the spec JSDoc at L1143–1149 carry the one wording ("keeps nothing to renew an access token it has to renew with (no refresh token was issued, or no client to refresh with)"); the card's "Done when" asked for exactly this convergence after PR #28955, which is on `main` at the merge base.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28961-connector-connection-status-doc.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. The diff publishes a changed comment in the emitted declarations and nothing else: no authorable key, value or type moves, so `none` is the kind and `patch` is its level. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from os-dev-report 6574504560 on the card (head `8d3ba747`) and the PR body:

- **Deviation: the first commit ran with `core.hooksPath` overridden, so `pre-commit` did not run; amended unpushed with the repo's `.githooks` before the first push.** Acceptable as declared: the pushed head is the only one that exists on the remote, it passed `pre-commit` and `pre-push` there, and every CI gate on it is green. Nothing to carry.
- **NOT MEASURED locally: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` (exit 3, prerequisite).** Both ride `Lint & Repo Gates`, green on this head. Right to leave to CI for a comment-only change.
- **`files_changed` and `line_budget` match the net diff** (2 files, 16 changed lines, no governed path).
- **File surface held:** the runtime (`packages/services/**`) is untouched, as the claim required; the runtime sentence it aligns to was already on `main` (PR #28955), so no wording waits on another PR.
- `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []` — nothing escalated, and this round found nothing the dev should have escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` only, every sentence the change writes against the runtime it describes. Attempts to break it:

- Tried to find a mark the three arms miss: every `markReconnectRequired` caller and every `reconnectRequiredReason` cause is covered (① item 3). Tried to find a `reconnect_required` written by the connect or revoke doors: neither writes the status; `revoke` deletes the row (the door then answers `not_connected`), `complete` upserts `connected`.
- Tried to read "no refresh token was issued" as also covering a read-back failure: it does not, by the store's own contract (① item 4).
- Tried to make "it has to renew" false for a connection that never needs a refresh: a connection whose server issued no refresh token is still refreshed on a cache miss or a 401 (① item 2), so the "has to renew" clause is what makes the sentence true without "expired". The runtime stores the same sense in both `no_refresh_token` and `no_client` reasons.
- Checked the rewrap moved no words other than the deletion of "expired" and the substitution "an access token it has to renew with": the three lines differ only by that edit and the wrap.

No must-fix, no should-fix. A note, not a finding: the JSDoc states the fact and the runtime's code comment states the mechanism (cache miss, moved revision, 401); a reader of the published contract gets the corrected fact without the mechanism, which is the right altitude for a status description and is what the card asked for.
